Breaking News.text:
BITCOIN SLIDES AS GEOPOLITICAL RISKS SPUR RISK-OFF TRADE

Bitcoin fell 1.7% to about $67,600 ahead of the U.S. open, tracking weaker equity futures. Nasdaq 100 futures dropped 0.9% and S&P 500 contracts lost 0.6%.

Investors are turning cautious amid rising tensions around Iran, fresh debate over AI’s broader economic impact, and uncertainty over Federal Reserve rate cuts after recent inflation data.

Flows remain negative: U.S.-listed Bitcoin ETFs saw a fourth straight week of outflows, with $360 million withdrawn last week. Sentiment is weak, with CryptoQuant’s Fear and Greed Index at 10 (“extreme fear”).

Analysts say Bitcoin may consolidate, with $60,000 viewed as key support. But further macro shocks could push prices back toward the $50,000s.
Breaking News.author: DeItaone

Breaking News.text:
IRAN OFFERS NUCLEAR CONCESSIONS, BUT STOPS SHORT OF ENRICHMENT BAN

Iran has floated new proposals in nuclear talks with the U.S., including pausing uranium enrichment for up to three years, sending part of its highly enriched uranium stockpile abroad—possibly to Russia—and pursuing future business deals if sanctions are lifted.

But Tehran has not agreed to fully halt enrichment, the key demand of President Donald Trump, who has called for dismantling Iran’s nuclear program while boosting U.S. military deployments in the region.

Talks in Geneva follow an earlier round in Oman. The U.S. is seeking strict limits on Iran’s nuclear activity, with additional pressure from Israel to curb Tehran’s missile program. Iran, meanwhile, wants meaningful sanctions relief, including access to billions in restricted oil revenues.

With Iran’s nuclear facilities damaged by strikes last June, analysts say Washington has little incentive to offer sweeping concessions—leaving a deal uncertain.

Breaking News.text:
U.S. TO EXPAND MISSILE DEPLOYMENTS IN PHILIPPINES, RAISING TENSIONS WITH CHINA

The U.S. Department of State said Washington will expand deployments of advanced missile and unmanned systems to the Philippines to deter China in the South China Sea.

The move reinforces the 1951 mutual-defense treaty after alliance talks in Manila. The U.S. previously deployed Typhon and NMESIS missile systems to the Philippines and signaled further additions, potentially during joint exercises in April.

Both sides reaffirmed that their treaty covers armed attacks on forces, aircraft and vessels.

Breaking News.text:
$NVDA - CITI: BUY NVIDIA AHEAD OF 2H26 OUTPERFORMANCE

Citigroup recommends adding to Nvidia, expecting the stock to outperform in the second half of 2026 as AI demand visibility improves into 2027.

Analyst Atif Malik forecasts January-quarter revenue of $67 billion (vs. $65.6 billion consensus) and April-quarter guidance of $73 billion (vs. $71.6 billion expected). A ramp in the B300 and Rubin platforms is projected to drive a 34% acceleration in second-half 2026 sales.

Investors are focused on Nvidia’s mid-March GTC conference, where the company is expected to outline its inference roadmap and provide early 2026–27 AI sales guidance.

Citi projects fiscal 2027 gross margins near 75%, with operating expenses rising in the high-30% range. While hyperscaler capex and inference competition are increasing, the bank believes Nvidia will remain the leader in both AI training and inference.

Citi reiterates its Buy rating and $270 price target, calling the stock attractive ahead of expected 2H26 strength.

Breaking News.text:
WEDBUSH: TECH SELLOFF OVERDONE AS AI SPENDING SURGES

The recent pullback in tech stocks is overdone, according to Wedbush Securities, which says the artificial intelligence investment cycle is still in its early innings.

The firm estimates the market is in year three of a decade-long AI buildout, with 2026 marking a key inflection point. It expects large tech companies to spend about $650 billion in capex in 2026, alongside growing government and corporate AI investment.

Recent volatility has hit major names despite strong earnings from Alphabet, Meta Platforms and Palantir Technologies. Wedbush views the weakness as short-term risk aversion, not a shift in long-term fundamentals.

The firm also argues that declines in Salesforce, ServiceNow and Microsoft fail to reflect their strategic roles in the AI ecosystem.

While AI is reshaping enterprise software budgets, Wedbush says fears of rapid displacement are overstated, and broader AI adoption should support sector growth.

INVESTORS SEE GOLD PEAKING AT $6,200

Investors in Bank of America’s February global fund manager survey expect gold to peak at $6,200 per ounce on a weighted-average basis.

One in five (20%) believe gold has already topped, while 19% see prices climbing above $7,000. Gold was trading at $4,937.40 per troy ounce on Tuesday morning.

Breaking News.text:
STRAIT OF HORMUZ PARTIALLY CLOSED FOR IRAN MILITARY DRILLS

Parts of the Strait of Hormuz will close for several hours Tuesday due to “security precautions,” according to Fars News Agency, as Iran’s Revolutionary Guards conduct military exercises.

The strait is the world’s most critical oil shipping chokepoint, linking major Gulf producers—Saudi Arabia, Iran, Iraq and the United Arab Emirates—to the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea.
